cards.text: God is still giving Moses instructions. Last time it was holy garments for Moses' brother Aaron and Aaron's sons (Exodus 28:1-4). Now God tells Moses how to consecrate them to serve Him as priests, starting with a young bull and two rams.

cards.question: For consecrating Aaron and his sons, God tells Moses to take a young bull and two rams. What must the animals be?

cards.text: Next, God tells Moses to fill a basket with unleavened bread, cakes mixed with oil and wafers anointed with oil, all made from fine wheat flour. Somebody's BAKING in Exodus, friend, and I just stood up a little taller on my base.

cards.question: Aaron and his sons are presented at the entrance to the Tent of Meeting. Before they're dressed, what is Moses to do to them?

cards.text: Then Moses is to dress Aaron in the tunic, the robe of the ephod, the ephod itself and the breastplate, with the ephod fastened on by its woven waistband. Me, I've got ONE apron, friend, and that thing does ALL the work.

cards.question: God tells Moses to put a turban on Aaron's head and attach the holy diadem to it.
With the turban on, Moses is to anoint Aaron by ___ the anointing oil on his head.

cards.text: Then Aaron's sons are presented and dressed in tunics, and Moses is to wrap sashes around Aaron and his sons and tie on headbands. Matching outfits for the whole crew, friend. That's a TEAM.

cards.question: God says the priesthood will belong to Aaron and his sons only for their own lifetimes.

cards.text: Now Moses is to present the young bull at the front of the Tent of Meeting. This ordination is NOT a handshake and a name tag, friend.

cards.question: The young bull stands at the front of the Tent of Meeting. Before it's slaughtered, what are Aaron and his sons to do?

answers.text: Lay their hands on its head

cards.text: Then the bull is slaughtered before the LORD at the entrance to the Tent of Meeting. Moses is to put some of its blood on the horns of the altar with his finger and pour out the rest at the base.
Next, Moses is to burn the fat covering the entrails, the lobe of the liver and both kidneys with their fat on the altar.

cards.question: The bull's fat and kidneys burn on the altar. Where are its flesh, hide and dung to be burned?

answers.text: At the foot of the mountain

cards.question: Burned outside the camp, the young bull is called a ___ offering.

cards.text: Next comes the first ram, and Aaron and his sons are to lay their hands on its head. Once it's slaughtered, Moses is to splatter its blood on all sides of the altar.

cards.question: Moses is to cut up the first ram, wash its entrails and legs, and burn only its fat on the altar.

cards.text: That first ram is burned whole, a burnt offering to the LORD, a pleasing aroma. Then the second ram comes up, and Aaron and his sons are to lay their hands on its head as well.

cards.question: Moses is to slaughter the second ram and put some of its blood on each priest's right earlobe and right thumb. Where else on the priests does it go?
Blood from the altar and anointing oil are to be sprinkled on Aaron and his sons, but not on their garments.

cards.text: The second ram is the ram for ordination, and Moses is to take its fat and right thigh along with one loaf, one cake made with oil and one wafer from the bread basket. I KNEW that basket was coming back, friend.

cards.question: Moses is to put the ram's fat and right thigh and the bread in the hands of Aaron and his sons. What does God tell Moses to do with them next?
After the wave offering, Aaron and his sons get to keep the waved fat and bread to eat themselves.
Moses is to wave the breast of the ordination ram before the LORD too. Whose portion does God say that breast will be?

cards.text: Moses gets a portion, and me, I get paid in crumbs, so GOOD for him. Then Moses is to consecrate the waved breast and the lifted thigh of the ordination ram for Aaron and his sons.

cards.question: That breast and thigh are a one-time gift to Aaron and his sons, just for their ordination day.

cards.text: Then God looks ahead: Aaron's holy garments will belong to his sons after him, so they can be anointed and ordained in them. Holy HAND-ME-DOWNS, friend.

cards.question: The son who succeeds Aaron as priest must wear the holy garments for ___ days.

cards.text: Back to the ordination ram: Moses is to boil its meat in a holy place, and Aaron and his sons eat it at the entrance to the Tent of Meeting with the bread from the basket. That basket is the MVP of this whole chapter, friend.

cards.question: God says no outsider may eat the ordination meat and bread. Why not?

answers.text: Because there isn't enough to share
Because it is only for the elders

cards.question: If any ordination meat or bread is left until morning, it must be ___ and not eaten.

cards.text: Leftovers? In MY bakery, a cookie has never once survived until morning, and every clue points to me. Moses is to take seven days to ordain them, with a bull sacrificed as a sin offering each day for atonement.

cards.question: Moses is to make atonement for the altar for seven days. Then whatever touches the altar will be ___.

cards.text: Then God gives the daily routine: two lambs a year old every day, one in the morning and one at twilight, each with fine flour, oil and wine. Morning AND twilight, every single day, friend, and some mornings I can't even beat my own snooze button.

cards.question: For the generations to come, this burnt offering is to be made at the entrance to the Tent of Meeting. What does God say will happen there?

cards.text: God says He'll meet with the Israelites there too, and that place will be consecrated by His glory. Then the LORD says He will consecrate the Tent of Meeting, the altar, and Aaron and his sons to serve Him as priests.

cards.question: Once everything is consecrated, God says He will dwell among the Israelites and be their God.
God says the Israelites will know He is the LORD their God who brought them out of Egypt. Why does He say He brought them out?

answers.text: So He might dwell among them
So they could build Him a city
So they could rule over Egypt

cards.text: And that's where we'll leave it for now, friend. God's not done giving Moses instructions, so keep that apron on.

findings.problem: Moses appears for the first time in the walkthrough, but the card doesn't say who he is. Aaron is introduced as Moses' brother, but Moses himself never is.

rule.text: New people. The first time someone shows up, he says simply who they are, like "Cyrus, king of Persia" or "Moses, Israel's leader."

findings.problem: The right answer "Without blemish" is the only one in biblical phrasing. The wrong answers "Born in the camp" and "Chosen by lot" are plain modern phrasing, so the right answer stands out.

rule.text: Don't let the right answer stand out. All the answers should sound alike. None should sound more like the Bible, or more modern, than the others.

findings.problem: The true or false about the turban and the holy diadem is pure recall of a detail no earlier card sets up. The baker can only guess.

rule.text: The check: could a thoughtful baker who has only seen the earlier cards make a reasoned pick? If the only way to get it right is luck, give the story card more context or ask a different question.

findings.problem: The blank asks the baker to guess the text's exact verb (pouring, rubbing or dabbing). That is wording they haven't seen, not meaning they can reason out.

rule.text: The rule against guessing the next words of a line (see below) applies to every passage, and to fill in the blank too. The blank tests meaning the baker can reason out, not wording they haven't seen.

findings.problem: The card says "Aaron's sons are presented and dressed in tunics," which sounds like an event that happened. Exodus 29:8 is God's command to Moses ("Present his sons as well and clothe them").

rule.text: Call things what the text calls them.

findings.problem: The card says "Then the bull is slaughtered before the LORD," which sounds like an event that happened. Exodus 29:11 is a command ("you shall slaughter the bull").

rule.text: Call things what the text calls them.

findings.problem: The card says "That first ram is burned whole," which sounds like an event that happened. Exodus 29:18 is a command ("Then burn the entire ram on the altar").

rule.text: Call things what the text calls them.

findings.problem: The card says "Aaron and his sons eat it," which sounds like an event that happened. Exodus 29:32 is a command ("Aaron and his sons are to eat").

rule.text: Call things what the text calls them.

findings.problem: Cards 12, 13, 16 and 18 are flat lists of ritual steps with no Papa Dorin voice. Card 13 especially is a bare list of organs burned on the altar.

rule.text: Short, but not stripped down. A story card still has enough of Papa Dorin's voice and enough context that the moment makes sense.

findings.problem: The question opens with "That breast and thigh," pointing back to the story card before it, which is no longer on screen. It doesn't say they come from the ordination ram.

rule.text: Always give context in the question. The story card before it isn't on screen anymore, so the question says who and what. Never "him," "that" or "it" pointing back to a card the baker can't see.

findings.problem: The right answer "Because these things are sacred" sounds more like the Bible than the casual, modern wrong answer "Because there isn't enough to share," so the right answer stands out.

rule.text: Don't let the right answer stand out. All the answers should sound alike. None should sound more like the Bible, or more modern, than the others.

findings.problem: Almost all of Exodus 29 is rules for offerings: the ordination sacrifices (29:1-37) and the daily offerings (29:38-41). The long-stretches section lists "rules for offerings and feasts" as a long stretch to sum up in one story card with no choice cards, and it says a stretch never gets a stop of its own. The walkthrough instead gives the ordination ritual about 35 cards, with choice cards on details like the right big toe, where the bull's hide is burned and who gets the breast.
findings.question: When nearly a whole passage is one of the long-stretch kinds (here, rules for offerings), should the ordination ritual be treated as a long stretch and summed up briefly, or as the heart of the passage with full story and choice cards? If it's a long stretch, what should Prep contain when the stretch is the whole passage?
